card.name: Past-tense words in historical narratives
card.fires_on: Words in the middle of a sentence about a past event, right after a dated or past-time phrase such as a year or 'had been'. Seen in history and biography text, mostly about 17th to 20th century people.

modes.description: The word right after a past date or year, starting a clause about what happened then.

modes.label: Past-event verbs and articles
modes.description: Helper verbs or articles in a past-tense account of a named person's earlier actions.
modes.example: His father had been<< a>> selectman and town representative decades before.

card.writes: It seems to lower words that point back to earlier times, such as 'later', 'at that time' and 'since', in Chinese and English.
card.plain: It fires on words in history passages that describe what someone did in a past year.
